title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 4 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Consecutive Number Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of numbers forms a consecutive sequence, with one number breaking that consecutive pattern
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers share a digit sum
Whether numbers are all perfect cubes
questions.rationale: This tests whether numbers form an unbroken consecutive sequence, identifying the one number that breaks the expected consecutive pattern.

questions.question: What does 'Arithmetic Pattern Classification' test?
options: Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers share a digit product
Whether a group of numbers follows a consistent arithmetic progression, with one number breaking that pattern
Whether numbers are all perfect squares
questions.rationale: This tests whether numbers follow a consistent arithmetic progression (constant difference), identifying the one number that doesn't fit that progression.

questions.question: What does a 'Square Difference Pattern' test?
options: A simple arithmetic progression
Whether the differences between consecutive numbers in a group follow a pattern related to squares
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers are all composite
questions.rationale: This tests whether the gaps between consecutive numbers follow a square-related pattern (like 1, 4, 9, 16...), identifying the value that breaks it.

questions.question: What does a 'Cube Pattern' test, similarly?
options: A square-based pattern
Whether numbers share a digit sum
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether a group of numbers or their differences follow a pattern related to cubes
questions.rationale: This tests whether numbers (or the differences between them) follow a cube-related pattern, identifying the value that breaks it.

questions.question: What does 'Fibonacci Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of numbers follows the Fibonacci sequence pattern, with one breaking it
A simple arithmetic pattern
Whether numbers are all prime
Whether numbers are all perfect squares
questions.rationale: This tests whether numbers follow the Fibonacci pattern (each number being the sum of the two before it), identifying the value that breaks this rule.

questions.question: What does 'Letter Classification' broadly test?
options: Only numeric properties
Only word meanings
Whether a group of letters (or words based on their letters) share a common alphabet-based property
A shared color
questions.rationale: Letter classification tests whether a group shares a common property based on the letters themselves, such as alphabet position or type.

questions.question: What does 'Vowel Classification' test?
options: Whether letters are all consonants
Whether a group of letters are all vowels, with one being a consonant (breaking the pattern)
Whether letters are all at odd positions
Whether letters are all at even positions
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of letters are all vowels (A, E, I, O, U), identifying the one letter that is actually a consonant.

questions.question: What does 'Consonant Classification' test, in contrast?
options: Whether letters are all vowels
Whether letters share a digit sum
Whether letters are all prime-positioned
Whether a group of letters are all consonants, with one being a vowel (breaking the pattern)
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of letters are all consonants, identifying the one letter that is actually a vowel.

questions.question: What does 'Alphabet Position Parity' classification test?
options: Whether letters are all vowels
Whether a group of letters all occupy odd (or all even) alphabet positions, with one breaking that pattern
Whether letters are all consonants
Whether letters share the same first letter
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of letters all share the same position parity (all odd-positioned or all even-positioned), identifying the exception.

questions.question: What does 'Alphabet Shift Classification' test?
options: A vowel/consonant distinction only
Whether a group of letter pairs share a consistent alphabet shift amount, with one pair breaking that consistent shift
A digit sum property
A prime number property
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of letter pairs are all related by the same consistent alphabet shift, identifying the pair that doesn't follow that same shift amount.
